name: World
features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

0. CLIENT RELATIONSHIPS THAT MATTER (player notes 22 Oct: favours such as an extra leg do nothing today; contracts should start poor and get better as you build relationships): every client has a visible relationship level (e.g. New → Known → Trusted → Partner) built by on-time flying, accepted change requests and favours (extra legs, short-notice cover, waiving a small penalty) and hurt by cancellations, sub-charters and late recoveries. Higher levels bring real rewards: better rates (+3–15 %), longer/bigger contracts, first refusal before rivals, faster payment, repeat and exclusive offers, forgiving small delays, and client-specific messages. A NEW COMPANY STARTS WITH POOR WORK (short, low-margin, odd hours, unloved routes, demanding clients) and better offers unlock as reputation and relationships grow. Show the level and its effect on each offer ('Trusted client: +8 % rate') and on a Clients view on the Company screen; plain-language card for why a client is unhappy.

9. MORE CONTRACT TYPES: Hajj airlifts (big seasonal pilgrim flights; dates drift ~11 days earlier each year with the Islamic calendar; max-seat cabins), UN multi-year rotations, VIP & presidential (high pay, high standards, premium cabins, extra crew), deportation flights (well paid; hurt reputation and crew morale — a moral choice), war-zone evacuations (war-risk insurance cost, danger, urgency), medical/air-ambulance style charters, music tours (multi-city routing), Antarctica flights (special approvals/runways). Each with realistic pay, requirements, feasibility explanations and flavour text with real clients.

10. RIVAL OPERATORS WITH PERSONALITIES: real ACMI operators (Hi Fly, Wamos Air, euroAtlantic, Getjet, Airhub, Avion Express, Titan Airways, Privilege Style, Air Atlanta Icelandic, Heston, KlasJet, Smartwings, Global Crossing...) each with a style (aggressive pricing, prestige, reliability, size), fleets that change over time, competing bids so the player sometimes loses work to a cheaper/closer rival (with an explanation), and sub-chartering BOTH ways (hire a rival when stuck; rivals ask the player to fly for them). A rivals view on the Company screen.

11. MARKET CYCLES: fuel price moves (affects charters/ferries and some offers), seasonality (summer peak, winter trough, Hajj season), and demand shocks (an airline collapse creates ACMI demand; recession lowers it); visible as a simple market outlook and in offer volume/pricing.

12. INVENTED WORLD EVENTS: coups, strikes, volcanic ash, natural disasters, airline failures, wars, airspace closures, etc. in real places involving real airlines/governments (the player explicitly wants invented events — BRIEF 'Player decisions'); they create urgent work (evacuations, AOG/ACMI demand), risks (airspace closures reroute or cancel flights, insurance) and opportunities, announced in the inbox and on the map (e.g. a shaded closed airspace).

13. DRY LEASE CONTRACTS (player request): the client leases the aircraft only — our pilots deliver it (ferry to the client's base, deadhead home on the map) and at the end collect it (deadhead out, ferry back); no crew from us during the lease; monthly lease income + hourly reserves; the client's hours accrue on our airframe (checks still ours, booked around the lease); the client may fly it in their own livery/paint (v0.5.1 paint); risk of late return / damage events. Feasibility and plain-language card.

14. MIXED-CREW CONTRACTS (player's real case: Getjet A330 for Air Senegal — 8 cabin crew, only 2 from Getjet): the client provides part or most of the CABIN CREW (never pilots): the contract says 'client provides N of M cabin crew' (half, most, all-but-the-purser...); our roster only fills our share (always at least the PUR unless the contract says the client's SCCM leads); lower price per block hour accordingly; morale/language/standards flavour; the roster board shows client crew as grey placeholder seats.

BASE (already released, in the tree): v0.7.3 In-flight Rest & EASA (pilot/cabin rest facilities per airframe, restPlan, EASA-FTL.md as the rules reference, extensions/split duty/standby/local nights/time zones, crew rest refits, ULR within 18 h) + v0.7.2.2 Check planning (drag A/C checks and refits along the timeline with live usage, idle-gap booking buttons, chainSane ferry clean-up) + v0.7.2.1 Trip swap (drag a whole trip between aircraft with a profit/loss confirm) on top of v0.7.2 Crew Rules & Fleet (PUR/CC, captain-as-FO, C-check MRO hubs, sale/early return, ops strip, real contract names) and v0.7.1 Crew Control (plain-language cards, <Term> glossary, WHY? buttons). Every new problem gets the four-line plain-language card. Add a v0.8 entry at the top of src/data/whatsNew.ts. Known leftovers to fold in if cheap: the bot's fleet() cash rule means no seed signs a widebody (loosen so 2–4 of 6 seeds do); bot runtime 32–35 s (target 12 s: profile and speed up); the Gantt shows 'free … nothing booked' beyond a base programme's generated days (label it as the programme continuing).
